ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r4.claim: On the certain Day of Judgment people cannot flee; foreheads expose sinners, who are seized and thrown into Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p110/r4.anchor: no evidence will be needed to convict a criminal as his forehead will bear witness to his sins. He will then be grabbed by his forehead and feet and flung into Hell.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p125/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p125/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p125/r1.claim: The denied questioning is investigative scrutiny: criminals need no interrogation because their faces disclose their crimes and deserved punishment; limbs and even hairs also testify.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p125/r1.anchor: the questioning which is refuted relates to investigation and scrutiny. At other places, the Qur’ ān has stated the reason why this would not be required

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p125/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p125/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p125/r2.claim: Questions of rebuke, reprimand, or sarcasm remain possible, so other Qur'anic reports of questioning criminals do not contradict this verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p125/r2.anchor: the questions which relate to rebuke, reprimand and sarcasm are concerned, they are not negated here. The questions which are mentioned in the Qur’ ān regarding the criminals are of this second type.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r1.claim: The tanwīn in fayaumʾidhin replaces a deleted clause, meaning the day when the sky split; the verse's negation of questioning is reconciled with verses affirming questions in different ways.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r1.anchor: فيومئذ: التنوين فيه للعوض من الجملة المحذوفة، والتقدير: فيوم إذ انشقت السماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r2.speaker: عكرمة وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r2.claim: ʿIkrima and Qatāda say questioning occurs at some stations but not others.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r2.anchor: فقال عكرمة وقتادة: هي مواطن يسأل في بعضها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās distinguishes questions of rebuke and confirmation from genuine inquiry about a sin, which God already knows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: حيث ذكر السؤال فهو سؤال توبيخ وتقرير، وحيث نفي فهو استخبار محض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r4.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r4.claim: Qatāda says questioning happened first, then mouths were sealed and hands and feet testified to people's deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة أيضا: كانت مسألة، ثم ختم على الأفواه وتكلمت الأيدي والأرجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r5.speaker: أبو العالية وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r5.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya and Qatāda say an innocent person is not asked about a sinner's wrongdoing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r5.anchor: وقال أبو العالية وقتادة: لا يسأل غير المجرم عن ذنب المجرم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r6.speaker: الحسن وعمرو بن عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan and ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd use an anomalous hamza reading in jānn to avoid the meeting of two silent letters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p66/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعمرو بن عبيد: ولا جأن بالهمز

RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r1.claim: One reading is that nobody asks them which person sinned, because their guilt is already recognized by blackened faces and other marks; the pronoun is explained by the following mention of humans and jinn.
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r1.anchor: لا يسأله أحد عن ذنبه ، فلا يقال : له أنت المذنب أو غيرك ، ولا يقال : من المذنب منكم

RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r2.claim: A second reading, close to 6:164, is that no sinful human or jinn is asked about their own sin; this raises a grammatical objection about the pronoun and the two agents.
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r2.anchor: وثانيهما : معناه قريب من المعنى قوله تعالى : { ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى } ( الأنعام : 164 )

RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r3.claim: To resolve the pronoun objection, one can treat “his sin” as an explicit noun phrase meaning a sinner’s sin, without a referential pronoun.
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما : أن لا يفرض عائدا وإنما يجعل بمعنى المظهر لا غير ويجعل عن ذنبه كأنه قال

RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r4.claim: The subtler, stronger grammatical solution places the pronoun’s antecedent before the verb: a sinner is not asked about his sin, whether human or jinn.
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r4.anchor: ثانيهما : وهو أدق وبالقبول أحق أن يجعل ما يعود إليه الضمير قبل الفعل فيقال : تقديره

RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r5.claim: The initial “then” may mark temporal succession after the sky splits, immediate logical succession as punishment starts without time for questioning, or rhetorical order after the failed attempt to escape through the heavens.
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r5.anchor: المسألة الأولى : اللفظية الفاء للتعذيب وأنه يحتمل أن يكون زمانيا كأنه يقول : فإذا انشقت السماء يقع العذاب

RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r6.claim: On the rhetorical-order reading, the warning first denies escape through the heavens, then says offenders will not even be given time to answer questions.
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#2/r6.anchor: وأقول لا تمتنعون عند انشقاق السماء ، فأقول : لا تمهلون مقدار ما تسألون

RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r1.claim: “Not asked” may mean no inquiry to identify the guilty, no rebuke asking why a sinner acted, or no request for pardon and intercession on another’s behalf.
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r1.anchor: المسألة الثانية : ما المراد من السؤال ؟ نقول : المشهور ما ذكرنا أنهم لا يقال لهم : من المذنب منكم

RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r2.claim: The intercession reading is challenged because “ask about” normally marks inquiry or reproach, while asking someone to grant something takes a direct object.
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r2.anchor: أحدها : أن السؤال إذا عدى بعن لا يكون إلا بمعنى الاستعلام أو التوبيخ وإذا كان بمعنى لاستعطاء

RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r3.claim: In reply, a verb of asking can take two objects; with inquiry the second is omitted and the following prepositional phrase states what information was requested.
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r3.anchor: السؤال ربما يتعدى إلى مفعولين غير أنه عند الاستعلام يحذف الثاني ويؤتى بما يتعلق به

RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r4.claim: The intercession reading can construe each human as not asking about another human’s sin; the pronoun is attached to the grammatical subject as in “they killed themselves,” though it does not mean each killed himself.
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r4.anchor: وعن الثاني : أن التقدير لا يسأل إنس ذنبه ولا جان ، والضمير يكون عائدا إلى المضمر لفظا لا معنى ، كما نقول

RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r5.claim: On that construal, no human or jinn is asked to pardon another; all petition God, and God alone is the one asked at that time.
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r5.anchor: فكذلك ( كل ) إنس لا يسأل ( عن ) ذنبه أي ذنب إنس غيره

RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r6.claim: An objection to the intercession reading is that the next verse’s statement that criminals are recognized by their marks does not fit it; al-Rāzī has supplied the grammatical and interpretive reply above.
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r6.anchor: ثالثها : قوله : { يعرف المجرمون بسيماهم } ( الرحمن : 41 ) لا يناسب ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r7.claim: The apparent conflict with 15:92 and 37:24 has two answers on the common reading: the afterlife has different stations, or the sinners are questioned reproachfully rather than for information; the latter is better.
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r7.anchor: أن للآخرة مواطن . فلا يسأل في موطن ، ويسأل في موطن

RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r8.claim: The stronger reconciliation says they are not asked to identify what they did, but are asked why the agent did it, as a rebuke; under the second interpretation there is no conflict to resolve.
RAZI-FULL:v29p104#3/r8.anchor: وثانيهما : وهو أحسن لا يسأل عن فعله أحد منكم ، ولكن يسأل بقوله : لم فعل الفاعل فلا يسأل سؤال استعلام ، بل يسأل سؤال توبيخ

RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r1.claim: On the common reading, the lack of questioning humiliates the guilty, like descriptions of faces covered with dust and gloom or blackened on Judgment Day.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r1.anchor: على الوجه المشهور فائدته التوبيخ لهم كقوله تعالى : { وجوه يومئذ * عليها غبرة * ترهقها قترة } ( عبس : 40 ، 41 )

RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r2.claim: On the second reading, the verse shows that no ransom is accepted; it completes the sequence denying escape in 55:33 and defense in 55:35.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r2.anchor: وعلى الثاني بيان أن لا يؤخذ منهم فدية ، فيكون ترتيب الآيات أحسن

RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r3.claim: On the intercession reading, the point is that no intercessor or merciful protector will be available to them.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r3.anchor: وعلى الوجه الأخير ، بيان أن لا شفيع لهم ولا راحم

RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r4.claim: Unlike worldly punishment, which God delays, afterlife punishment is not postponed even for the time needed to ask a question.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r4.anchor: وفائدة أخرى : وهو أنه تعالى لما بين أن العذاب في الدنيا مؤخر بقوله : { سنفرغ لكم }

RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r5.claim: After escape and defense are ruled out, wrongdoers cannot hope to hide in an unnoticed crowd: every sinner will be exposed, unlike a small group that might escape worldly punishment by obscurity.
RAZI-FULL:v29p105/r5.anchor: وهو أن يقول المذنب : ربما أنجو في ظل خمول واشتباه حال ، فقال : ولا يخفى أحد من المذنبين بخلاف أمر الدنيا

STUDYQURAN:55:39/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:39/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:39/r1.claim: The verse parallels 28:78 and 77:35–36: the guilty are not questioned and cannot speak or make excuses; their deeds are already recorded, as in 17:71, 18:49, 50:17–18, 69:19–28, and 82:11–12.
STUDYQURAN:55:39/r1.anchor: None shall be questioned that day, since their deeds have already been recorded

STUDYQURAN:55:39/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:39/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:39/r2.claim: On that Day people cannot speak for themselves: mouths are sealed, hands and feet testify to deeds, and ears, eyes, and skins testify against them, as in 36:65 and 41:20.
STUDYQURAN:55:39/r2.anchor: Their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to that which they used to earn (36:65)

STUDYQURAN:55:39/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:39/r3.speaker: Aj, IK
STUDYQURAN:55:39/r3.claim: Some reconcile this verse with 15:92–93 by saying people will first be questioned and then have their mouths sealed.
STUDYQURAN:55:39/r3.anchor: some say that they will be questioned, and then their mouths will be sealed (Aj, IK)

STUDYQURAN:55:39/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:39/r4.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:55:39/r4.claim: Another explanation is that questioning is rhetorical reproach, not an attempt to elicit an answer.
STUDYQURAN:55:39/r4.anchor: they will not be questioned in order to elicit a response, but only rhetorically, as a form of reproach (Aj)

STUDYQURAN:55:39/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:39/r5.speaker: Sufi perspective
STUDYQURAN:55:39/r5.claim: After the lower self is effaced through annihilation and subsistence in God, no sin remains because one can only act according to God's Will.
STUDYQURAN:55:39/r5.anchor: when the attributes of the lower self have been effaced, after one has passed through the stations of both annihilation and subsistence in God

BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r1.claim: They are not asked about sin because their signs already identify them; this is at the first stage, as they leave their graves and arrive in groups at the gathering place, whereas questioning and accounting occur at another station.
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r1.anchor: لأنهم يعرفون بسيماهم فلا يحتاج في تمييز المذنب عن غيره إلى أن يسأل عن ذنبه

BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r2.claim: The statement that all will be questioned applies to the station of examination and accounting, reconciling it with this verse's denial of questioning at the initial gathering.
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r2.anchor: وأما قوله فوربك لنسألنهم أجمعين ونحوه ففي موقف المناقشة والحساب

BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says they are not asked whether they did particular deeds, since God knows them, but why they did them.
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لا يسألهم هل عملتم كذا وكذا فإنه أعلم بذلك منهم

BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r4.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says the questioning is not for comfort and relief; rather, it is interrogation to reproach and rebuke.
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r4.anchor: وعنه أيضا ويسألون سؤال شفاء وراحة وإنما يسألون سؤال تقريع وتوبيخ

BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r5.claim: The pronoun in 'his sin' returns to humans because they precede jinn in rank; the singular means an individual human, and al-jānn refers to jinn as a whole.
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r5.anchor: وضمير ذنبه للإنس لتقدمه رتبة وأفراده لما أن المراد فرد من الإنس

BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r6.claim: Inwardly, lights of obedience shine on the pages of the spirit-human, while sins pile darkness, tyranny, and disobedience onto the face and neck of the rebellious, dark self.
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r6.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى شعاشع أنوار الطاعة والعبادة على صفحات وجنات إنس الروح وإلى تراكم ظلمات المعصية

BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r7.claim: God's gifts to the obedient and vengeance on the defiant are both blessings; punishment of enemies benefits the beloved, and complete vengeance annihilates the traits of the commanding self.
BURSEVI:v9p247#2/r7.anchor: فإن الانتقام من الأعداء نعمة على الأحباب ولذا ورد الحمد عقيبه كما قال تعالى فقطع دابر القوم الذين ظلموا

TABATABAI:55:31-39/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r1.claim: This second section describes the second creation, return to God, and recompense, recalling divine favors; the preceding first section described the first creation and its favors.
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r1.anchor: هذا هو الفصل الثاني من آيات السورة يصف نشأة الثقلين الثانية وهي نشأة الرجوع إلى الله وجزاء الأعمال

TABATABAI:55:31-39/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r2.claim: To ‘be free for’ someone is to leave other tasks and focus attention on that matter; ‘We shall attend to you’ means the present creation will end and God will turn to the two groups.
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r2.anchor: يقال فرغ فلان لأمر كذا إذا كان مشتغلا قبلا بأمور ثم تركها وقصر الاشتغال بذاك الأمر اهتماما به

TABATABAI:55:31-39/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r3.claim: The next verses explain this attention as resurrection, reckoning, and recompense for good or bad deeds; ‘attend to you’ is an implicit metaphor for the change of creation.
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r3.anchor: وتبين الآيات التالية أن المراد بالاشتغال بهم بعثهم وحسابهم ومجازاتهم بأعمالهم خيرا أو شرا

TABATABAI:55:31-39/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r4.claim: This ‘attending’ does not conflict with God’s not being distracted by one affair from another: it concerns a change of creation, while non-distraction concerns the reach of divine power; neither conflicts with God being in a new affair each day.
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r4.anchor: ولا ينافي الفراغ لهم كونه تعالى لا يشغله شأن عن شأن

TABATABAI:55:31-39/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r5.claim: The two weighty groups are jinn and humans; plural pronouns address them because each group contains many individuals.
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r5.anchor: والثقلان الجن والإنس، وإرجاع ضمير الجمع

TABATABAI:55:31-39/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r6.claim: The address to jinn and humans is a challenge on Judgment Day: if able, escape through the regions of heaven and earth and leave God’s dominion and accountability.
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r6.anchor: من خطابات يوم القيامة وهو خطاب تعجيزي

TABATABAI:55:31-39/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r7.claim: Ability means power, escape through the regions means fleeing, and aqṭār is the plural of quṭr, meaning a direction or region; jinn are mentioned first because they move faster.
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r7.anchor: والمراد بالاستطاعة القدرة، وبالنفوذ من الأقطار

TABATABAI:55:31-39/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r8.claim: ‘Unless with authority’ means escape is possible only with some kind of dominion; sulṭān can mean existential power, proof or any argument, or kingship.
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r8.anchor: أي لا تقدرون على النفوذ إلا بنوع من السلطة

TABATABAI:55:31-39/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r9.claim: An alternative takes the denied escape as scientific penetration into the heavens and earth, but al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the context does not fit that reading.
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r9.anchor: وقيل المراد بالنفوذ المنفي في الآية النفوذ العلمي

TABATABAI:55:31-39/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r10.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r10.claim: Al-Rāghib defines shawāẓ as flame without smoke; al-Majmaʿ describes it as a green flame fragment breaking away from fire, close to that sense.

TABATABAI:55:31-39/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r11.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r11.claim: Al-Majmaʿ glosses nuḥās as smoke, while al-Rāghib gives it as a flame without smoke; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the meaning is clear.
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r11.anchor: والنحاس الدخان وقال الراغب هو اللهب بلا دخان والمعنى ظاهر

TABATABAI:55:31-39/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r12.claim: ‘You will not help one another’ means they cannot support each other to escape the suffering, since causes lose their effect and there is no protector from God that day.
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r12.anchor: أي لا تتناصران بأن ينصر بعضكم بعضا لرفع البلاء والتخلص عن العناء لسقوط تأثير الأسباب ولا عاصم اليوم من الله

TABATABAI:55:31-39/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r13.claim: When heaven splits it becomes rose-red like red leather.
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r13.anchor: أي كانت حمراء كالدهان وهو الأديم الأحمر

TABATABAI:55:31-39/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r14.claim: This verse and the following verses describe Judgment’s reckoning and reward, the condition of criminals, and those who fear their Lord’s station and their outcomes.
TABATABAI:55:31-39/r14.anchor: الآية وما يتلوها من الآيات إلى آخر السورة تصف الحساب والجزاء

TABATABAI:55:41-43/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r1.claim: The reckoning is swift, as Qur’an 14:51 says; the negated question is the familiar form of questioning and does not conflict with other verses that affirm questioning.
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r1.anchor: ثم الآية تصف سرعة الحساب وقد قال تعالى والله سريع الحساب

TABATABAI:55:41-43/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:41-43/r2.claim: The question is denied at some stations, while other stations include questioning, sealed mouths, speaking limbs, and recognition by marks; hence Qur’an 37:24 and 15:92 do not contradict this verse.

TABRISI:55:37-45/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:37-45/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:37-45/r9.claim: In that particular scene, criminals are not questioned because bewilderment overwhelms them; questioning occurs at another time, as 37:24 shows.
TABRISI:55:37-45/r9.anchor: أي لا يسأل المجرم عن جرمه في ذلك الموطن لما يلحقه من الذهول الذي تحار له العقول

TABRISI:55:37-45/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:37-45/r10.speaker: قول آخر
TABRISI:55:37-45/r10.claim: They are not questioned to discover their deeds, since God has recorded them; rather, questioning is for rebuke and accounting.
TABRISI:55:37-45/r10.anchor: سؤال استفهام ليعرف ذلك بالمسالة من جهته لأن الله تعالى قد أحصى الأعمال

TABRISI:55:37-45/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:37-45/r11.speaker: قول آخر
TABRISI:55:37-45/r11.claim: Since people of Paradise and Hell are recognizable by their faces, they need not be asked which group they belong to; their deeds are questioned in rebuke.
TABRISI:55:37-45/r11.anchor: إن أهل الجنة حسان الوجوه وأهل النار سود الوجوه فلا يسألون من أي الحزبين هم

TABRISI:55:37-45/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:37-45/r12.speaker: الرضا
TABRISI:55:37-45/r12.claim: Al-Rida says a person who believed the truth, sinned, and did not repent is punished in the barzakh, then arrives on Resurrection Day with no sin to be asked about.
TABRISI:55:37-45/r12.anchor: وروي عن الرضا ع أنه قال: فيومئذ لا يسأل منكم عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r1.claim: People are not questioned to discover their sins or distinguish sinners from others; they are questioned instead for rebuke and blame.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r1.anchor: يعني: لا يسأل ليعرف ذلك بالمسألة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r2.claim: Muqātil says they are not asked because God has already enumerated their deeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r2.anchor: وهذا معنى قول مقاتل: لا يسأل لأن الله قد أحصى عمله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والعوفي عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and al-ʿAwfī from Ibn ʿAbbās say angels recorded the deeds, so people are not asked what they did but why they did it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r3.anchor: قالوا: لا يسألون ليعرف ذلك من جهتهم، لأن الملائكة قد كتبت عليهم أعمالهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r4.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r4.claim: Mujāhid says they are not questioned to identify criminals, since their marks identify them, as 55:41 says.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لا يسألون ليعرف المجرمون فإنهم يعرفون بسيماهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r5.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r5.claim: ʿIkrima says there are some stations where they are questioned and others where they are not.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r5.anchor: وقال عكرمة: إنها مواقف يسأل في بعضها ولا يسأل في بعضها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r6.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r6.claim: Al-Kalbī says the verse concerns the period after the accounting has ended.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r6.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هذا الفراغ من الحساب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba adopts the post-accounting view: people are questioned during the long Judgment Day, then speech and dispute cease and groups are known by their faces.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r7.anchor: واختار ابن قتيبة هذا القول وشرحه فقال: إن يوم القيامة كما قال الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r8.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj’s view is that people are not asked an information-seeking question about their sins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r8.anchor: أحدها: لا يسألون سؤال استفهام عن ذنوبهم، وهو اختيار الزجاج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r9.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ’s view is that people are not questioned in order to identify them by their sins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p177/r9.anchor: والثاني: لا يسألون ليعفروا بذنوبهم وهو اختيار الفراء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179/r1.claim: Muqātil glosses the pair as a human and a jinni.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: يقول إنسي ولا جني

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179/r2.speaker: ثعلب عن عمرو عن أبيه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179/r2.claim: Thaʿlab, citing ʿAmr from his father, says al-jānn is one of the jinn and its plural is jinān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p179/r2.anchor: قال ثعلب، عن عمرو، عن أبيه: الجان من الجن وجمعه جنان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:33-41/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:33-41/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:33-41/r7.claim: This is not a question seeking information; the guilty are questioned to reproach and rebuke them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:33-41/r7.anchor: { فيومئذ لا يسأل عن ذنبه } سؤال استفهام، ولكن يسألون سؤال تقريع وتوبيخ.

QASHANI:55:33-40/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:33-40/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:33-40/r1.claim: Human beings are the outward-oriented and jinn the inward-oriented; neither is questioned when each is drawn to its station and home by its dominant original or acquired disposition.
QASHANI:55:33-40/r1.anchor: من الباطنيين لانجذاب كل إلى مقره ومركزه وموطنه

QASHANI:55:33-40/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:33-40/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:33-40/r2.claim: The stopping and questioning mentioned elsewhere occur at other times during the long Day, when neither side of a person's nature has prevailed.
QASHANI:55:33-40/r2.anchor: ففي مواطن أخر من اليوم الطويل الذي كان مقداره خمسين ألف سنة

QASHANI:55:33-40/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:33-40/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:33-40/r3.claim: There is no questioning when original light and capacity remain, or when dark traits have become entrenched and capacity has vanished; questioning belongs to the intermediate state where traits obstruct return but are not fixed beyond recovery.
QASHANI:55:33-40/r3.anchor: وفي وقت استيلاء الهيئات الظلمانية وترسخ الغواشي الجسمانية وزوال الاستعداد الأصلي بحصول الرين لا يسئلون

QASHANI:55:33-40/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:33-40/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:33-40/r4.claim: Intermediate souls are questioned and punished according to their sins and the traits' entrenchment; as acquired states extinguish innate capacity, it resists gradually, producing torments until the forces balance, and questioning can follow renewed readiness.
QASHANI:55:33-40/r4.anchor: حتى يعذبوا بحسب سيئاتهم على قدر رسوخها

QASHANI:55:33-40/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:33-40/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:33-40/r5.claim: The eternally wretched and the spiritually fortunate who enter the Garden without reckoning are never stopped or questioned.
QASHANI:55:33-40/r5.anchor: فلا يسئلون قط ولا يوقفون للسؤال

QASHANI:55:33-40/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:33-40/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:33-40/r6.claim: The command to stop them in 37:24 applies specifically to some punished people whose final outcome is release from punishment.
QASHANI:55:33-40/r6.anchor: مخصوص ببعض المعذبين، وهم الأشقياء الذين عاقبتهم النجاة من العذاب

ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r55.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r55.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r55.claim: Not asking about sin does not cancel reckoning or responsibility: the guilty are not questioned to discover whether they are criminals, since they are already identified and are not confused with the innocent.
ELMALILI:55:26-45#2/r55.anchor: ne ins ne de cânn günahından

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r1.claim: After the scene of the Resurrection, humans and jinn are not asked about sins, sinners are hauled to Hell and made to enter and leave its fire, then fall into boiling water without relief.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r1.anchor: 37. âyetin ardından insanlara ve cinlere günahları hakkında soru sorulmayacağı, günahkârların yaka paça cehenneme atılacakları ve inkâr edip durdukları bu gerçeği iyice bellemeleri için cehennem ateşine sokulup çıkarılacakları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r2.claim: The verse does not mean that there will be no questioning in the afterlife; rather, people's states will be so clear that they need not give their own account.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r2.anchor: Şu var ki, 39. âyetteki “İşte o gün ... günahı hakkında soru sorulmaz” anlamındaki ifadeyi, “âhirette sorgu olmayacak” diye anlamamak gerekir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r3.claim: Their deeds are recorded, their tongues, hands, and feet testify, and sinners are recognized by their faces, so no declaration is needed to establish their condition.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r3.anchor: herkes dünyada yapıp ettiklerinin tek tek kayda geçirilmiş olduğunu görecek, günahkârların dilleri, elleri ve ayakları bu konuda tanıklık edecek, ayrıca 41. âyette ifade edildiği gibi günahkârlar simalarından tanınacaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r4.claim: After each person is gathered according to their deeds, judgment begins; God gives everyone a thorough hearing despite knowing all, to show justice and mercy and let each recognize and affirm the fate they deserve.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:37/r4.anchor: herkes kendi sevap ve günah durumuna göre haşrolunup hesap meydanına getirildikten sonra yargı süreci başlayacak; yüce Allah, bütün kullarının iyilik ve kötülüklerini eksiksiz kusursuz bilmesine rağmen adalet ve şefkatini ortaya koymak

BURHAN:v3p256/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p256/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p256/r7.claim: Humans are often mentioned before jinn; the order may foreground the more astonishing creation, since jinn's creation is stranger.
BURHAN:v3p256/r7.anchor: ومنه تقديم الإنس على الجن في قوله

BURHAN:v2p8/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p8/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p8/r1.claim: Prohibition can be inferred from explicit bans, threats, blame, expiation, phrases such as لا ينبغي, penalties, or descriptions of an act as corrupt or hated by God.
BURHAN:v2p8/r1.anchor: ويستفاد التحريم من النهي والتصريح بالتحريم والحظر

BURHAN:v2p8/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p8/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p8/r2.claim: Permissibility can be inferred from permission or choice, an order after a ban, no burden or blame, divine pardon or provision, and uncondemned practice.
BURHAN:v2p8/r2.anchor: ويستفاد الإباحة من الإذن والتخيير والأمر بعد الحظر ونفي الجناح والحرج والإثم والمؤاخذة والإخبار بأنه يعفو عنه

BURHAN:v2p8/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p8/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p8/r3.claim: If a report of an act is paired with praise, that is evidence the act is recommended or obligatory rather than merely permissible.
BURHAN:v2p8/r3.anchor: فإن اقترن بإخباره مدح دل على رجحانه استحبابا أو وجوبا

BURHAN:v2p8/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p8/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p8/r6.claim: An act is legally sanctioned at least as obligatory or recommended when God or the Messenger praises, loves, approves, rewards, protects, forgives, announces security for, or swears by it or its agent.
BURHAN:v2p8/r6.anchor: وكل فعل عظمه الله ورسوله أو مدحه أو مدح فاعله لأجله أو أحبه أو أحب فاعله

BURHAN:v2p53/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p53/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p53/r1.claim: In analogy, claiming the same cause both to establish a ruling and to produce its opposite is contradictory; a distinction that adds to the cause reveals it was inadequately defined.
BURHAN:v2p53/r1.anchor: فكل من أوجد علة وحررها وأوجب بها حكما من الأحكام

BURHAN:v2p53/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p53/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p53/r2.claim: Only possible questions merit answers; asking whether someone can be standing upright and sitting at once is an impossible question, whose terms can instead be explained.
BURHAN:v2p53/r2.anchor: إما أن يسأل فيما يستحق الجواب عنه أو لا

BURHAN:v2p53/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p53/r5.speaker: الحليمي
BURHAN:v2p53/r5.claim: Al-Ḥalīmī reconciles the questioning passages by distinguishing questions about monotheism and messengers from questions about religious laws and branches.
BURHAN:v2p53/r5.anchor: قال الحليمي فتحمل الآية الأولى على السؤال عن التوحيد وتصديق الرسل والثانية على ما يستلزم الإقرار بالنبوات

BURHAN:v2p53/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p53/r6.speaker: غيره
BURHAN:v2p53/r6.claim: Another explanation distinguishes the many resurrection settings: some involve questioning, scrutiny, mercy, or admonition; believers are not rebuked as disbelievers are.
BURHAN:v2p53/r6.anchor: حمله غيره على اختلاف الأماكن لأن في القيامة مواقف كثيرة فموضع يسأل ويناقش وموضع آخر يرحم

ITQAN:v2p547#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r4.claim: A pronoun may precede its matching antecedent in wording while the antecedent is not later in syntactic rank, as in these examples.
ITQAN:v2p547#2/r4.anchor: أو متأخرا لفظا لا رتبة مطابقا نحو ﴿ فأوجس في نفسه خيفة موسى ﴾ ﴿ ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون ﴾

ITQAN:v3p76/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p76/r1.speaker: الزركشي
ITQAN:v3p76/r1.claim: Different descriptions of Adam's creation refer to successive states, not contradiction: dust develops through altered mud and clinging clay to pottery-like dried clay.
ITQAN:v3p76/r1.anchor: قال الزركشي في البرهان للإختلاف أسباب

ITQAN:v3p76/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p76/r2.speaker: الزركشي
ITQAN:v3p76/r2.claim: Moses' staff is called a great serpent for its form, but likened to a small snake for its rapid, light movement.
ITQAN:v3p76/r2.anchor: قال الزركشي في البرهان للإختلاف أسباب

ITQAN:v3p76/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p76/r3.speaker: الحليمي
ITQAN:v3p76/r3.claim: Al-Halimi reconciles verses that affirm and deny questioning by assigning the first questions to belief in God's oneness and the messengers, and the second to religious laws and their details.
ITQAN:v3p76/r3.anchor: قال الحليمي فتحمل الآية الأولى على السؤال عن التوحيد وتصديق الرسل والثانية على ما يستلزمه الإقرار بالنبوات

ITQAN:v3p76/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p76/r4.speaker: غيره
ITQAN:v3p76/r4.claim: Another explanation is that the Resurrection has many stations: people are questioned at some and not at others.
ITQAN:v3p76/r4.anchor: وحمله غيره على اختلاف الأماكن لأن في القيامة مواقف كثيرة ففي موضع يسألون وفي آخر لا يسألون

ITQAN:v3p76/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p76/r5.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v3p76/r5.claim: A further explanation distinguishes questioning for reproach, which occurs, from questioning to seek an excuse or establish proof, which does not.
ITQAN:v3p76/r5.anchor: وقيل إن السؤال المثبت سؤال تبكيت وتوبيخ والمنفى سؤال المعذرة وبيان الحجة

ITQAN:v3p76/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p76/r6.speaker: الشيخ أبو الحسن الشاذلي
ITQAN:v3p76/r6.claim: Al-Shadhili reads the command to fear God as fully due as a command about monotheism, supported by the following words about dying as Muslims, and reads the other command as concerning deeds.
ITQAN:v3p76/r6.anchor: حمل الشيخ أبو الحسن الشاذلي الآية الأولى على التوحيد بدليل قوله بعدها

ITQAN:v3p76/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p76/r7.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v3p76/r7.claim: An alternative says the command to fear God as fully due was abrogated by the command to fear Him as far as one is able.

ITQAN:v3p76/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p76/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p76/r8.claim: The apparent conflict about justice between wives is resolved by distinguishing fair fulfillment of rights, which is possible, from emotional inclination, which people cannot control.
ITQAN:v3p76/r8.anchor: والجواب أن الأولى في توفية الحقوق والثانية في الميل القلبي وليس في قدرة الإنسان

ITQAN:v4p340#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p340#2/r1.speaker: الغزالي
ITQAN:v4p340#2/r1.claim: Al-Ghazali and others count five hundred Qur'anic legal verses, while some count only 150; they may mean explicit rulings, since stories and parables also yield legal inferences.
ITQAN:v4p340#2/r1.anchor: قال الغزالي وغيره آيات الأحكام خمسمائة آية وقال بعضهم مائة وخمسون قيل ولعل مرادهم المصرح به

ITQAN:v4p340#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p340#2/r2.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين بن عبد السلام
ITQAN:v4p340#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salam says most Qur'anic verses contain rulings through manners and ethics; rulings may be explicit or inferred, sometimes from one verse and sometimes by combining verses, such as a six-month minimum pregnancy.
ITQAN:v4p340#2/r2.anchor: معظم آي القرآن لا يخلوا عن أحكام مشتملة على آداب حسنة وأخلاق جميلة ثم من الآيات ما صرح فيه بالأحكام

ITQAN:v4p340#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p340#2/r3.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين بن عبد السلام
ITQAN:v4p340#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salam says rulings are indicated by legal wording, statements of permission or prohibition, or promised worldly and otherworldly benefits and harms; praise, love, acceptance, guidance, reward, forgiveness, safety, nearness, light, healing, and similar signs show a deed is either obligatory or recommended.
ITQAN:v4p340#2/r3.anchor: ويستدل على الأحكام تارة بالصيغة وهو ظاهر وتارة بالإخبار مثل

FARRA:v3p116/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p116/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p116/r11.claim: Neither human nor jinn is asked because they are recognized by signs: the disbeliever's black face and blue eye, the believer's radiant wudu-marked limbs.
FARRA:v3p116/r11.anchor: لأنهم يعرفون بسيماهم كما وصف الله: فالكافر يعرف بسواد وجهه، وزرقة عينه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p46/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p46/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p46/r1.claim: The verses are reconciled by stages in the long Day of Judgment: people are questioned at presentation, then after the case is settled speech and dispute end, faces are marked, and books are distributed.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p46/r1.anchor: ففي مثل هذا اليوم يسألون وفيه لا يسألون، لأنهم حين يعرضون يوقفون على الذنوب ويحاسبون

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p46/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p46/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p46/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse describes one particular station at which people are not questioned.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p46/r2.anchor: وكذلك قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r2.speaker: قالوا
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r2.claim: The objectors allege a contradiction between saying no human or jinn is asked about sin and saying God will question everyone about their deeds.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r2.anchor: وقالوا: وهل التناقض إلا مثل قوله: فيومئذ لا يسئل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان

NAHHAS:v4p312/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p312/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p312/r1.claim: The phrase on that day is the answer to idhā.

NAHHAS:v4p312/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p312/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p312/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says they are not questioned to test them, since God has preserved a record of their deeds.
NAHHAS:v4p312/r2.anchor: قول ابن عباس لا يسألون سؤال اختبار لأن الله جل وعز قد حفظ عليهم أعمالهم

NAHHAS:v4p312/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p312/r3.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v4p312/r3.claim: Qatada says they are recognized by black faces and blue eyes, as the following verse indicates.
NAHHAS:v4p312/r3.anchor: وقول قتادة أنهم يعرفون بسواد الوجوه وزرق الأعين ويدل على هذا أن بعده

SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r1.claim: The tanwin in يومئذ substitutes for إذ انشقت السماء; the fāʾ is the conditional apodosis.
SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r1.anchor: التنوين عوض من الجملة، أي: فيوم إذ انشقت السماء. والفاء في " فيومئذ " جواب الشرط.

SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r2.claim: Alternatively, the condition’s answer is omitted, with an understood terrifying event when the sky splits.
SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو محذوف، أي: فإذا انشقت السماء رأيت أمرا مهولا

SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r3.claim: The pronoun in ذنبه returns to either human or jinn; the other is elided, with لا يسأل عن ذنبه جان also understood.
SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r3.anchor: والهاء في " ذنبه " [تعود على أحد المذكورين]. وضمير الآخر مقدر، أي: ولا يسأل عن ذنبه جان أيضا.

SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r4.claim: لا يسأل governs the time adverb, and لا does not prevent government; the author refers to disagreement at al-Fātiḥa.
SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r4.anchor: وناصب الظرف " لا يسأل " و " لا " غير مانعة. وقد تقدم خلاف الناس فيها في الفاتحة.

SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r5.claim: A hamzated reading جأن had already been discussed for جان.
SAMIN-DURR:55:39/r5.anchor: وتقدمت قراءة " جأن " بالهمز فيها أيضا.

ZAJJAJ:v5p100/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p100/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p100/r9.claim: Zajjāj juxtaposes no one being asked with the command to question people; criminals are recognized by black faces and blueness, supported by 55:41, 3:106, and 20:102.
ZAJJAJ:v5p100/r9.anchor: فإذا كان ذلك اليوم كانت سيما المجرمين سواد الوجه والزرقة

ASAD-NOTES:55:39#n19/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:39#n19/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:39#n19/r1.claim: Sinners need not be questioned because their deeds will confront them in the record and their own tongues, hands, and feet will testify to what they did.
ASAD-NOTES:55:39#n19/r1.anchor: I.e., the sinners "will find all that they ever wrought [nowl facing them" (18:49)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p265/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p265/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p265/r1.claim: Al-Hasan explains that people are not questioned because God has preserved their deeds.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p265/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ لا يسأل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان ﴾ قال قد حفظ الله عليهم أعمالهم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r1.claim: On the day the sky splits, no one is asked because people are recognized by their signs; verses that affirm questioning concern another station, according to Ikrima and Qatadah.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r1.anchor: لأنهم يعرفون بسيماهم وهذا في موقف وما دل على السؤال

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r2.claim: One explanation places questioning at the reckoning and says questioning is absent when people emerge from their graves.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r2.anchor: وموقف السؤالأعلى ما قيل : عند الحساب وترك السؤال

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes affirmations of questioning as rebuke and reproach from negations of questioning as genuine inquiry about the sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : حيث ذكر السؤال فهو سؤال توبيخ وتقدير وحيث نفي فهو استخبار محض

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r4.claim: Another reconciliation says the denied question concerns the sin itself while the affirmed question concerns its cause; the author objects that verses affirm questioning about the sin itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : المنفي هو السؤال عن اذلنب نفسه والمثبت هو السؤال عن الباعث عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r5.speaker: الطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r5.claim: Al-Tabarsi attributes to al-Rida the view that an unrepentant sinner who believed the truth is punished in the intermediate realm and reaches Judgment Day with no sin to be questioned about.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r5.anchor: وحكى الطبرسي عنالرضا رضي الله تعالى عنه أن من اعتقد الحق ثم أذنب ولم يتب عذب في البرزخ

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r6.claim: The author emphatically rejects attributing that explanation to al-Rida and says the verse should not be forced into it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r6.anchor: ولعمري إن الرضا لم يقل ذلك وحمل الآية عليه مما لا يلتفت إليه بعين الرضا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r7.claim: The pronoun in ذنبه refers to إنس, which is prior in grammatical rank as the passive subject; the singular pronoun follows its grammatical form.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r7.anchor: وضمير ذنبهللإنس وهو متقدم رتبة لأنه نائب عن الفاعل وإفراده باعتبار اللفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r8.claim: An alternative explains the singular pronoun by taking the intended referent to be one individual from humankind.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r8.anchor: وقيل : لما أن المراد فرد من الإنس

ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r9.speaker: الحسن، عمرو بن عبيد
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r9.claim: Al-Hasan and Amr ibn Ubayd read ولا جأن with hamza to avoid the meeting of two vowelless letters, though the sequence is otherwise permitted by the rule.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p114#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعمرو بن عبيد ولا جأن بالهمز فرارامن التقاء الساكنين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r9.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r9.claim: Ḥasan and Qatāda say sinners are not questioned to discover their sins: God already knows them and angels recorded them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r9.anchor: قال الحسن وقتادة: لا يسئلون عن ذنوبهم لتعلم من جهتهم، لأن الله عز وجل علمها منهم، وكتبت الملائكة عليهم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r10.claim: Al-ʿAwfī's report from Ibn ʿAbbās gives the same explanation: their sins need not be elicited because God knows and they are recorded.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r10.anchor: وهي رواية العوفي عن ابن عباس (2) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says angels do not question sinners because they recognize them by their marks; Mujāhid agrees, with the following verse as evidence.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r11.anchor: وهي رواية العوفي عن ابن عباس (2) . وعنه أيضا: لا تسأل الملائكة المجرمين لأنهم يعرفونهم بسيماهم. دليله: ما بعده، وهذا قول مجاهد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reconciles this with 15:92: they are not asked whether they committed an act, since God knows, but why they did it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r12.anchor: وعن ابن عباس في الجمع بين هذه الآية وبين قوله: "فوربك لنسئلنهم أجمعين"، (الحجر -92) ، قال: لا يسألهم هل عملتم كذا وكذا؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r13.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r13.claim: ʿIkrima says there are different stations: people are questioned at some and not at others.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r13.anchor: وعن عكرمة أنه قال: إنها مواطن، يسأل في بعضها ولا يسأل في بعضها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they are not questioned with compassion or mercy, but rather to rebuke and reproach them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p449#2/r14.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا: لا يسألون سؤال شفقة ورحمة وإنما يسألون سؤال تقريع وتوبيخ

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:37-42/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:37-42/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:37-42/r5.claim: No human or jinn is questioned because their marks reveal their sins as they emerge from graves and arrive in groups at the gathering, according to their ranks.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:37-42/r5.anchor: لأنهم يعرفون بسيماهم وذلك حين ما يخرجون من قبورهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:37-42/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:37-42/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:37-42/r6.claim: This does not conflict with verses about questioning: questioning occurs at the gathering for reckoning, whereas this verse describes their earlier arrival; the pronoun refers to al-ins by grammatical gender.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:37-42/r6.anchor: فحين يحاسبون في المجمع، والهاء للإنس باعتبار اللفظ

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:37-42/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:37-42/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:37-42/r7.claim: The repeated question about God's favors refers here to what He grants His believing servants on that Day.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:37-42/r7.anchor: أي مما أنعم الله على عباده المؤمنين في هذا اليوم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r10.claim: The criminals are not questioned to discover what they did; questioning is instead reproach, as in asking why they acted so.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r10.anchor: سؤال تعرف واستعلام بل سؤال تقريع وتوبيخ وكلام

BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r11.claim: The eschatological day is long and has changing phases: in some periods people are questioned and in others they are not.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r11.anchor: ذلك اليوم طويل , وهو ذو ألوان تارة يسأل فيه وتارة لا يسأل

BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r12.claim: Qur’an 75:30 uses “that day” for the time when the soul reaches the collarbones, a period not bounded by ordinary night and day.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r12.anchor: أي يوم إذا بلغت الروح التراقي وهو لا يختص بليل ولا نهار

BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r13.claim: The passive construction magnifies the matter and indicates that the sinner’s condition is publicly knowable across every era.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r14.claim: The singular pronoun focuses the question on each person’s particular sin; the virtuous are questioned about good deeds to honor them and admonish those below.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r14.anchor: وقد سئل المحسن عن حسنته سؤال تشريف له وتنديم لمن دونه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r15.claim: Humans are named first because they are the main focus, their messenger was human, and familiar witnessed examples teach most clearly; jinn are added to show all are easy for God.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p390/r15.anchor: ولما كان الإنس أعظم مقصود بهذا , ولهذا كان الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم

DURR-FULL:v7p702/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p702/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p702/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says God will not ask whether people did particular deeds because He already knows; instead, He will ask why they did them.
DURR-FULL:v7p702/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {فيومئذ لا يسأل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان} قال: لا يسألهم هل عملتم

DURR-FULL:v7p702/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p702/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p702/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says people will not be asked about their deeds or one another, comparing this with 28:78 and 2:119.
DURR-FULL:v7p702/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {فيومئذ لا يسأل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان} يقول: لا أسألهم عن أعمالهم

DURR-FULL:v7p703/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r1.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r1.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet’s statement about judgment and forgiveness, and that a Muslim sees his deeds in the grave, citing this verse.
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r1.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: لا

DURR-FULL:v7p703/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r2.claim: Mujahid says angels need not question criminals because they recognize them by their marks.
DURR-FULL:v7p703/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {فيومئذ لا يسأل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان} قال: لا تسأل الملاكئة عن المجرم يعرفونهم بسيماهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r4.claim: It establishes the creation of jinn and their accountability, then turns from annihilation to resurrection and requital.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r4.anchor: وخلق الجن وإثبات جزائهم . والموعظة بالفناء وتخلص من ذلك إلى التذكير بيوم الحشر والجزاء .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r8.claim: Other Qur'anic passages affirm questioning in the Hereafter, while this verse and others deny it; the apparent tension needs reconciliation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r8.anchor: وفي القرآن آيات تقتضي أن في القيامة سؤالا، وآيات تقتضي نفيه كهذه وغيرها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r9.speaker: قتادة وعكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r9.claim: Qatāda and ʿIkrima reconcile the passages by assigning questioning and its absence to different stages or occasions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r9.anchor: فقال بعض الناس ذلك في مواطن دون مواطن، وهو قول قتادة وعكرمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, the author's preferred view, says an affirmed question means reproach and eliciting acknowledgment; negation means genuine inquiry, which God does not need.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وهو الأظهر في ذلك أن السؤال متى أثبت فهو بمعنى التوبيخ والتقرير، ومتى نفي فهو بمعنى الاستخبار المحض والاستعلام، لأن الله تعالى عليم بكل شيء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r11.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid say the angels do not ask about the criminals because they recognize them by their marks.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p231#2/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد: لا يسأل الملائكة عنهم، لأنهم يعرفونهم بالسيما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118/r1.claim: One Ibn ʿAbbās view says they are not questioned to learn their state, since God already knows it.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118/r2.claim: A second Ibn ʿAbbās view says people do not question one another about their condition because each is preoccupied with himself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118/r2.anchor: لا يسأل بعضهم بعضا عن حاله لاشتغال كل واحد منهم بنفسه روي القولان عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says they are not asked about their sins because their faces identify them: unbelievers’ faces are black, while believers are marked by the radiance of ablution.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118/r3.anchor: لا يسألون عن ذنوبهم لأنهم يعرفون بسيماهم فالكافر أسود الوجه والمؤمن أغر محجل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj clarifies that they are not asked to find out their sins; rather, the questioning is a rebuke.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p118/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج لا يسأل أحد عن ذنبه ليستفهم ولكنه يسأل سؤال توبيخ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r1.claim: Not being asked describes one state; in another, everyone is questioned about all deeds, as 77:35–36 says no speech or permission to offer excuses, while 15:92–93 says all will be questioned.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r1.anchor: فهذا في حال، وثم حال يسأل الخلائق فيها عن جميع أعمالهم، قال الله تعالى:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r2.claim: Qatada says there was questioning, then mouths were sealed and hands and feet testified to what people had done.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God does not ask whether they committed a deed, since He knows it, but asks why they did it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r3.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: لا يسألهم: هل عملتم كذا وكذا؟ لأنه أعلم بذلك منهم، ولكن يقول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r4.claim: Mujahid says the angels do not ask about a criminal, since they recognize him by his marks.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد في هذه الآية: لا يسأل الملائكة عن المجرم، يعرفون بسيماهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r5.claim: The third view fits the stage after criminals are ordered to the Fire: they are no longer asked about sins but driven and thrown into it, as 55:41 describes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p499/r5.anchor: لا يسألون عن ذنوبهم، بل يقادون إليها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r5.claim: إنس means some humans and جان means some jinn; the ancestor's name is used for descendants, and the singular pronoun reflects the meaning some of humankind.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r5.anchor: إنس } بعض من الإنس { ولا جان } أريد به : ولا جن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r6.claim: They are not asked because their marks identify them as criminals: black faces and blue eyes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r6.anchor: وإنما وحد ضمير الإنس في قوله : { عن ذنبه } لكونه في معنى البعض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r7.claim: Although 15:92 and 37:24 say people will be questioned, the Day has different stations where they are or are not asked.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r7.anchor: فإن قلت : هذا خلاف قوله تعالى : { فوربك لنسئلنهم أجمعين }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r8.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r8.claim: Qatada says questioning occurred, then mouths were sealed and hands and feet spoke about people's deeds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r8.anchor: قال قتادة : قد كانت مسألة ، ثم ختم على أفواه القوم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r9.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r9.claim: Another view says they are not asked to discover their sins, but are questioned in reproach.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r9.anchor: وقيل لا يسأل عن ذنبه ليعلم من جهته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r10.speaker: الحسن وعمرو بن عبيد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r10.claim: Al-Hasan and Amr ibn Ubayd read ولا جأن with an added alif to avoid adjacent vowelless letters.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p449/r10.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعمرو بن عبيد ( ولا جأن ) فرارا من التقاء الساكنين

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r10.claim: Questioning happened earlier; later mouths are sealed and hands and feet testify to what people did.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r10.anchor: كانت المسألة قبل , ثم ختم على أفواههم وتكلمت أيديهم وأرجلهم بما كانوا يعملون , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r11.claim: It means they will not be asked whether they committed a particular act.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r11.anchor: لا يسألهم هل عملتم كذا وكذا , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r12.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r12.claim: The angels are not asked about people because they already raised their deeds in worldly life.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r12.anchor: لا يسأل الملائكة عنهم لأنهم قد رفعوا أعمالهم في الدنيا , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r13.claim: People do not ask one another about their condition because each is preoccupied with himself.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r13.anchor: بنفسه , وهذا مروي عن ابن عباس أيضا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r14.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r14.claim: Contrasting face colors identify people, so they need not be asked.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p435#2/r14.anchor: فهم معروفون بألوانهم فلم يسأل عنهم ، قاله الفراء

MUJAHID:v2p642#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p642#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p642#4/r1.claim: Mujahid says the angels do not question humans or jinn about their sin because they recognize the criminals by their marks, echoing 55:41.
MUJAHID:v2p642#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ فيومئذ لا يسأل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان ﴾ يقول لا تسأل الملائكة عن المجرم

MUQATIL:55:38-40/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:38-40/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:38-40/r1.claim: No human or jinn is asked about their deeds because God has already recorded them.
MUQATIL:55:38-40/r1.anchor: لأن الرب تعالى قد أحصى عليه عمله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p203#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p203#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p203#8/r1.claim: On the day the sky splits, no human or jinn is asked about his sin; jan, literally the father of the jinn, stands for the jinn, as Hāshim can stand for his descendants.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p203#8/r1.anchor: ﴿ لا يسأل عن ذنبه انس ولا جان ﴾ اى ولا جن فوضع الجان الذى هو أبو الجن موضع الجن

NASAFI-FULL:v4p203#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p203#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p203#8/r2.claim: Nasafi reconciles this with the oath that all will be questioned (15:92); Qatāda says questioning occurred before mouths were sealed and hands and feet testified (36:65). Another explanation says they are not questioned to discover their guilt, but are questioned reproachfully.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p203#8/r2.anchor: والتوفيق بين هذه الآية وبين قوله وفوربك لتسألنهم اجمعين

QURTUBI-FULL:55:37-39/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:37-39/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:37-39/r13.claim: Al-Qurtubi links this to the verse saying wrongdoers will not be asked about their sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:37-39/r13.anchor: هذا مثل قوله تعالى: ولا يسأل عن ذنوبهم المجرمون

QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r1.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r1.claim: One explanation is that people are not questioned after settling in Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r1.anchor: وقيل: المعنى لا يسألون إذا استقروا في النار

QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r2.claim: Hasan and Qatada say sins are not asked about because God and the angels recorded them; al-ʿAwfi transmits this from Ibn ʿAbbas.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة: لا يسألون عن ذنوبهم لأن الله حفظها عليهم

QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r3.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r3.claim: They say angels do not need to ask because they recognize people by their marks, as the next verse explains.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r3.anchor: وعن الحسن ومجاهد أيضا: المعنى لا تسأل الملائكة عنهم لأنهم يعرفونهم

QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reconciles this with the oath that all will be questioned: God does not ask to learn deeds but asks why as rebuke.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r5.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya says the innocent are not asked about a guilty person's sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r5.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: لا يسأل غير المجرم عن ذنب المجرم

QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r6.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r6.claim: Qatada says questioning happened earlier; then mouths are sealed and bodily limbs testify.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: كانت المسألة قبل ثم ختم على أفواه القوم

QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r7.claim: A Prophetic hadith describes people denying they will meet God; a hypocrite's mouth is sealed and his limbs testify to his deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r7.anchor: وفي حديث أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفيه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r8.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r8.claim: Ikrima says Resurrection has stages over its long duration: people are questioned at some times and not others.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:39/r8.anchor: وأن القيامة مواطن لطول ذلك اليوم فيسأل في بعض ولا يسأل في بعض،
